definition: What a tag of a sound is, and how a tag filter reads it. A tag is normalised in three steps, in this order: surrounding whitespace is removed, the text is lowercased, and a tag left empty is dropped. Accents are kept (`Intérieur` becomes `intérieur`, never `interieur`), whitespace inside a tag is kept as typed, and nothing else changes the text. Whitespace is the Unicode White_Space property and lowercasing is the Unicode default lowercase mapping, character by character, with no accent folding and no Unicode normalisation form applied. A list of tags is normalised tag by tag, then a tag already seen earlier in the list is dropped: the first occurrence stays and the order of the list is kept. `sound.tags` is the list as typed. `tags` is the normalised list, the only field the tag filter and the name search read. A tag filter is a list of tags, normalised the same way. It matches a sound when the filter is empty once normalised (no filter keeps every sound) or when at least one tag of the filter is among the normalised tags of the sound. `matches` is the answer to that filter; it is true when `filter` is absent.

tags.rule: each tag trimmed, lowercased and non-empty; no tag twice; order of first occurrence kept

matches.rule: true when the normalised filter is empty, else true exactly when a tag of the normalised filter is in tags
